A tracking camera monitors an object with harmonic position x(t) = {A} cos(t). The camera angle is θ(x) = arctan(x). At time t₀ = arcsin({x_disp}), the object is at x₀ = x(t₀) with velocity dx/dt = {dxdt_d}. Find the camera's angular velocity dθ/dt.

An oscillating particle has position x(t) = {A} cos(t). At time t₀ = ∫₀^{b} {c}/({csq} + x²) dx, its position is x₀ = x(t₀). Let m be the slope of the curve y = arctan(x) at x = x₀. Evaluate ∫₀^m e^({k}x) dx.

In the partial fraction decomposition of {A}/((x − {p})(x − {q})), let b be the absolute value of the numerator of 1/(x − {p}). A spindle is formed by rotating the region under a curve y = f(x) from x = 0 to x = b about the x-axis. In evaluating the cross-sectional integral ∫₀^b [f(x)]² dx by parts, the boundary term is ∫₀^b x^{n} dx and the remaining integral ∫ v du equals {iv}. Find the exact volume of the solid generated.

In the partial fraction decomposition of {A}/((x − {p})(x − {q})), let M be the numerator of 1/(x − {p}), and set b = |M| + 1. If I = ∫₁^b (1/x) dx, and a population grows according to dy/dt = e^t with initial value y(0) = {y0}, find the population y(I).
In the partial fraction decomposition of {A}/((x − {p})(x − {q})), let M be the numerator of 1/(x − {p}), and set b = |M| + 1. With I = ∫₀^b x dx and J = ∫₁^(1+I) (1/x) dx, evaluate ∫₀^J e^({k}x) dx.

Let θ = arcsin({x_disp}). A solid of revolution is generated by rotating the region under a curve y = f(x) about the x-axis. In evaluating the integral ∫ [f(x)]² dx using integration by parts, the boundary evaluation is ∫₀^θ sin²(x) dx, and the remaining integral ∫ v du equals {iv}. If the solid's cross-sectional area is scaled by a factor of {C}, find the resulting volume of revolution.

Let θ = arccos({x_disp}). In an integration by parts evaluation of an integral, the boundary evaluation is ∫₀^θ cos²(x) dx and the integral ∫ v du equals {iv}, yielding a net value J. Find the slope of the curve y = arcsin(x) at x = J/{scale}.

A particle moves in simple harmonic motion with displacement x(t) = {A} cos(t). At time t₀ = ∫₀^{b} 1/√({csq} − x²) dx, its displacement is x₀ = x(t₀). A tracking sensor measures viewing angle θ(x) = arctan(x). If the particle moves with horizontal speed dx/dt = {dxdt_d}, producing angular rate v, and an accumulator satisfies dz/dt = v with initial value z(0) = {z0}, find z({T}).

An optical tracking system monitors a particle with harmonic displacement x(t) = {A} cos(t). At time t₀ = arccos({x_disp}), the particle has position x₀ = x(t₀). The sensor angle is θ(x) = arctan(x). When dx/dt = {dxdt_d}, producing angular speed v, evaluate ∫₀^v x^{n} dx.

In the partial fraction decomposition of {A}/((x − {p})(x − {q})), let b be the numerator of 1/(x − {p}). The region under y = x^(n/2) from x = 0 to x = b is rotated about the x-axis to form a spindle of volume V. In an integration by parts calculation, the boundary term is V and the remaining integral ∫ v du equals {iv}, giving net cross-sectional value J. A reservoir level satisfies dy/dx = g(x) with initial level y(0) = {y0} and net inflow ∫ g(x) dx = J. Find the final level y.

Let θ = arctan({x_disp}). In an integration by parts calculation, the boundary evaluation is ∫₀^θ sin²(x) dx and the integral ∫ v du equals {iv}, yielding net value J. A quantity grows according to dy/dx = e^({k}x) with y(0) = {y0}. Find y(J).

A particle moves along the curve F(x, y) = 0 where ∂F/∂x = {Fx} and ∂F/∂y = {Fy}. The tangent slope of the curve is u, and the slope of the curve y = arcsin(x) at x = u is m. With horizontal speed dx/dt = {dxdt_d}, producing vertical rate v, an integration by parts calculation has boundary evaluation v and second integral ∫ v du equal to {iv}, giving net cross-sectional area J. Find the volume of the solid generated by rotating this region about the x-axis.

A quality control test yields margin of error E for z = {z}, s = {s}, and n = {n_val}. A test oscillator has displacement x(t) = {A_disp} cos(t), reaching x₀ = x(E). Let m be the slope of the curve y = arcsin(x) at x = x₀. When the oscillator moves with horizontal speed dx/dt = {dxdt_d}, producing rate v, a reservoir level satisfies dw/dt = v with w(0) = {w0}. The level w({T}) forms the cross-sectional profile integral ∫₀^b [f(x)]² dx of a solid of revolution. Find the volume of this solid.

A pendulum has release angle θ₁ = arcsin({x_disp}), reaching horizontal position x₀ = {A} cos(θ₁). The transit time across this distance is θ₂ = ∫₀^x₀ 1/√({csq} − x²) dx. The energy transmission integral is I = ∫₀^θ₂ sin²(x) dx. A cylindrical solid of revolution is formed by rotating this energy profile about the axis. If fluid is added to a container having initial level y(0) = {y0} by an amount equal to the solid's volume, find the final level in the container.

A contour track follows F(x, y) = 0 where ∂F/∂x = {Fx} and ∂F/∂y = {Fy}. A vehicle moves along the track with horizontal speed dx/dt = {dxdt_d}, producing vertical speed v. The work rate parameter is I = ∫₀^v x^{n} dx. In an integration by parts calculation, the boundary term is I and the remaining integral ∫ v du equals {iv}, giving net cross-sectional integral J. A hydraulic chamber is formed by rotating this profile about the axis. If the chamber already contains an initial reserve volume y(0) = {y0}, find the total fluid volume when completely filled.

Let θ = ∫₀^{b} 1/√({csq} − x²) dx. The slope of the curve y = arcsin(x) at x = θ/{scale} is m. With horizontal speed dx/dt = {dxdt_d}, producing rate v, an integration by parts calculation yields boundary term v and second integral ∫ v du equal to {iv}, giving net value J. A chemical concentration satisfies dc/dx = 1/x for x ≥ 1 with c(1) = {c0}. Find c(5 + J).
